knowledge:
- key_parameters: bamfiles=List of BAM files for single-cell samples ;; file=Path to a multiplexed 10x Genomics BAM file ;; sites=Genomic coordinates to count variants from (e.g., "chrM:1-15000") ;; ncores=Number of threads for parallel processing ;; ignore_nonstandard=Logical to ignore basecalls other than A, G, C, T, or N ;; min.af/MINFRAC=Minimal allele frequency for a site to be considered mutant in a single cell ;; lim.cov/MINREADS=Minimum number of reads overlapping a site in a single cell to be considered covered ;; universal.var.cells=Number/fraction of cells that must be mutant for a variant to be filtered out (e.g., germline mutations) ;; min.num.samples/MINCELL=Minimum number of cells that must be mutant for a variant to be included ;; exclusionlists=Named list of GRanges objects containing genomic coordinates of variants to exclude ;; patient=Vector indicating patient/sample origin for cohort-based filtering ;; method=Tree-building method in varCluster ("SCITE" or "PhISCS") ;; min.lik=Parameter controlling the merging of mutations into clones in clusterMetaclones
- alternatives: SCITE vs PhISCS for phylogenetic tree computation (PhISCS requires Gurobi and gurobipy, while SCITE does not require licenses but may need manual compilation) ;; mutationCallsFromExclusionlist (for single samples) vs mutationCallsFromCohort (preferred/more powerful when multiple individuals/samples are available to filter shared technical/biological noise)
- when_to_use: When analyzing single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, or DNA-seq data to identify clonal populations using somatic mitochondrial mutations.
- pitfalls: Mitochondrial genome lengths and sequences differ between references (e.g., UCSC hg19 is 16571 bp, hg38 is 16569 bp, mm10 is 16299 bp); ensure the sites parameter and reference genome match the BAM file annotations ;; Default exclusion lists are relative to 'hg38' coordinates and must not be used with other genomes without a liftOver step ;; PhISCS requires an external Gurobi license and python environment setup ;; The tree-building step (varCluster) can be slow (e.g., ~4 minutes for a small dataset).

workflows.name: variant_calling_from_bam
workflows.intent: Extract base counts from single-cell BAM files and call high-confidence mitochondrial variants using exclusion lists or cohort-based filtering.
input: cell_bams/ (directory of single-cell BAM files) OR multiplexed_10x.bam (10x Genomics multiplexed BAM file)
workflows.stages: 1. Count nucleotides from BAM files using baseCountsFromBamList or bam2R_10x ;; 2. Call and filter mutations using mutationCallsFromExclusionlist (for single samples) or mutationCallsFromCohort (for cohorts) ;; 3. Perform quick clustering and visualization using quick_cluster.
workflows.code:
baseCounts <- baseCountsFromBamList(bamfiles = list(system.file("extdata", "mm10_10x.bam", package="mitoClone2")), sites="chrM:1-15000", ncores=1)
baseCounts <- bam2R_10x(file = system.file("extdata", "mm10_10x.bam", package="mitoClone2"), sites="chrM:1-15000", ncores=1)
Example <- mutationCallsFromExclusionlist(example.counts, min.af=0.05, min.num.samples=5, universal.var.cells = 0.5 * length(example.counts), binarize = 0.1)
Example.rawnames <- getAlleleCount(Example,'nonmutant')
Example.meta <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(Example.rawnames), Clone = gsub("_.*","",gsub("Donor1_","",rownames(Example.rawnames))))
clustered <- quick_cluster(Example, binarize = TRUE, drop_empty = TRUE, clustering.method = "ward.D2", annotation_col = Example.meta, show_colnames=FALSE,fontsize_row = 7)
Example <- mutationCallsFromCohort(example.counts, MINFRAC=0.01, MINCELL=8, MINCELLS.PATIENT=5, patient = Example.meta$Clone, sites='chrM:1-55')
private.mutations <- unique(unlist( lapply(Example[grep('^C',names(Example))][unlist(lapply( Example[grep('^C',names(Example))],function(x)!is.null(x)))], function(y) names(getVarsCandidate(y))) ))
private.mutations.df <- pullcountsVars(example.counts, gsub("X(\\d+)([AGCT])\\.([AGCT])","\\1 \\2>\\3",private.mutations))
private.mutations.df <- mutationCallsFromMatrix(t(private.mutations.df$M), t(private.mutations.df$N), cluster = rep(TRUE, length(private.mutations)))
clustered <- quick_cluster(private.mutations.df, binarize = TRUE, drop_empty = TRUE, clustering.method = "ward.D2", annotation_col = Example.meta,show_colnames=FALSE,fontsize_row = 7)

workflows.name: clonal_clustering_and_tree_building
workflows.intent: Build a phylogenetic tree of mitochondrial mutations and cluster them into clones.
workflows.stages: 1. Load count matrices and create mutation calls using mutationCallsFromMatrix ;; 2. Build a phylogenetic tree using varCluster with SCITE or PhISCS ;; 3. Cluster mutations into metaclones and assign cells using clusterMetaclones ;; 4. Plot the clones using plotClones ;; 5. Optionally overwrite metaclone assignments manually using getMut2Clone and overwriteMetaclones.
workflows.code:
load(system.file("data/M_P1.RData",package = "mitoClone2"))
load(system.file("data/N_P1.RData",package = "mitoClone2"))
P1 <- mutationCallsFromMatrix(as.matrix(M_P1), as.matrix(N_P1))
tmpd <- tempdir()
dir.create(paste0(tmpd,'/p1'))
P1 <- varCluster(P1, tempfolder=paste0(tmpd,'/p1'),method='SCITE')
P1 <- clusterMetaclones(P1, min.lik = 1)
plotClones(P1)
m2c <- mitoClone2:::getMut2Clone(P1)
m2c[c("X2537GA","X14462GA")] <- as.integer(6)
P1.new <- mitoClone2:::overwriteMetaclones(P1, m2c)
plotClones(P1.new)
